text: Planet radius koi_prad estimates the radius of a planet candidate, usually in Earth radii. Planet size can help distinguish planetary signals from false positives.
Signal to noise ratio koi_model_snr measures the strength of the transit signal relative to noise. A stronger signal can make a transit easier to detect, but it does not prove that a planet exists.
Orbital period koi_period is the time required for an object to complete one orbit around its star, measured in days. Repeated transits help estimate this period.
Transit duration koi_duration measures how long a transit event lasts, in hours. It depends on factors including orbital geometry and the sizes of the star and transiting object.

Transit depth koi_depth measures the decrease in observed stellar brightness during a transit, commonly reported in parts per million. It provides information about the relative sizes of the object and its star.

Equilibrium temperature koi_teq is an estimated temperature based on the balance between absorbed stellar energy and emitted thermal energy under assumed conditions. It is not the measured surface temperature.
Insolation koi_insol represents the stellar energy received by a planet candidate relative to the Earth's solar irradiance. It helps characterize the candidate's radiation environment.

A false positive is an astronomical signal that appears planet-like but is determined not to be a genuine planet. Examples include eclipsing binary stars and other astrophysical or instrumental signals.
An exoplanet candidate is an object whose observations are consistent with a possible planet but that has not yet been confirmed. Additional validation may be required.
